status: DRAFT written by Claude, NOT yet reviewed by a domain person. Edit freely; every line is a plain-English guess at how people phrase things.
purpose: Maps the technical terms of the ontology (property and kind names) to the everyday words people use in questions, so a question can be matched to the right relation by meaning. Not used by the pipeline yet.
how_to_review: For each entry: does 'means' say what the relation is in this data? Do the phrases sound like something a user would type? Delete wrong phrases, add missing ones, and fix anything where two entries could be confused.

containsDrug.means: A brand is made of a drug (its active ingredient).

targetedIndication.means: A brand is aimed at a disease or condition (its indication).
phrases: what illness does the brand address

inTherapeuticArea.means: A brand, an indication or a document belongs to an area of medicine (for example Oncology, Cardiology, Immunology).
phrases: which field does it belong to

hasDrugClass.means: A drug belongs to a class of drugs, usually named by how it works.
phrases: what type of drug is it

company.means: The company that makes or owns a brand. A plain text value, not a separate entity.

competesWithin.means: Two brands are compared against each other in the same competitive landscape document.

coMentionedWith.means: Two brands are named in the same passage of a document. About text, not about the market.
phrases: named in the same passage as

hasSentiment.means: A brand has recorded opinions (sentiment assertions) from market research.

forBrand.means: A sentiment assertion is about one brand.
phrases: which brand is this opinion about

forGeography.means: A sentiment assertion was measured in one country or region.
phrases: how does sentiment differ across regions

forIndication.means: A sentiment assertion is about one disease or condition.

sentimentScore.means: The number (0 to 1) that says how positive a sentiment assertion is. A plain value.

mentionsBrand.means: A document or passage names a brand.
phrases: documents that talk about the brand

mentionsDrug.means: A document or passage names a drug.
phrases: documents that talk about the drug

mentionsDrugClass.means: A passage names a drug class.
phrases: where is the class of drugs discussed

mentionsIndication.means: A document or passage names a disease or condition.

coversGeography.means: A document or passage is about a country or region.
phrases: which countries does the document cover

isChunkOf.means: A passage (chunk) comes from one document.
phrases: which document is this passage from
where does this snippet come from

documentTitle.means: The title of a document. A plain value.

study_type.means: The kind of research a document is (for example survey, interview, landscape). A plain value.
phrases: is it a survey or an interview

quality_score.means: How good the document is judged to be by the ingestion checks. A plain value.

containsDocument.means: A knowledge space holds a document.
phrases: which documents are in the knowledge space

spaceName.means: The name of a knowledge space. A plain value.

partOfRegion.means: A country belongs to a larger region (for example a country in the EU).
phrases: which region is the country in

subIndicationOf.means: A disease is a narrower form of a broader disease.

Brand.means: A product sold under a trade name.

Drug.means: The active ingredient inside a brand.

DrugClass.means: A group of drugs that work in the same way.

Indication.means: A disease or condition a brand is aimed at.

MarketResearchDocument.means: A report, survey or interview summary that was ingested.

DocumentChunk.means: A short passage cut from a document.

SentimentAssertion.means: One recorded opinion with a score.

KnowledgeSpace.means: A collection of documents scoped to a team or area.

notes_for_reviewer: 'medicine' is used both for a brand (what a patient buys) and for a drug (the ingredient). It is listed under containsDrug only; decide whether that is right.

'competitor' is taken to mean competesWithin (compared in a competitive landscape document). 'mentioned together' is coMentionedWith (same passage). These are different things in the data; check the wording separates them.
'region' is listed under Geography. EU and APAC are Geography entries too, linked from countries by partOfRegion.
'HCP' means healthcare professional; the sentiment entries cover how HCPs view a brand.
Left out on purpose: bookkeeping relations (lineage, review, index ids, access labels). Questions are not asked about those through the graph.
No synonyms were added for brand or drug NAMES. Those come from the data catalog.
